name: drift-tube-pressure-gradient
description: Closed form: the uniform transit L / (mu E) scaled by the mean density along the path, because mobility goes as the reciprocal of density and the transit is therefore the integral of n(x) dx over mu_ref n_ref E. The mean of a linear ramp is the average of its ends, so 1.5. A 38 mm drift tube whose gas thickens along it, from 1 mbar where the packet starts to 2 mbar at the detector. This is what a differentially pumped instrument looks like, and until a pressure field could be imported it was not expressible: a model could declare a neutral velocity everywhere and only ever the same number of neutrals everywhere. GAS-1 asks for both. THE EXPECTED NUMBER IS AN INTEGRAL THIS ENGINE HAS NO PART IN. An ion drifts further between collisions in a thinner gas, so it is mu times n that is constant - which is why the literature tabulates REDUCED mobility - and the drift speed is therefore mu_ref n_ref E / n(x). The transit is the integral of dx over that, which is the integral of n(x) dx divided by mu_ref n_ref E: the uniform answer scaled by the MEAN density along the path. For a linear ramp that mean is the average of the two ends, so 1.5 mbar against a declared 1 mbar, and 0.09 m^2/(V s) in 2 kV/m is 180 m/s, so 38 mm at uniform 1 mbar takes 211.1 us and this takes 1.5 times that. The mobility is declared rather than derived, per TRN-1, which is also what keeps the expectation arithmetic. The unit is required on the file for the reason section 9 requires it on a scalar: vacuum work is quoted in mbar and torr at least as often as in pascals, and a file read as pascals when it holds mbar is a gas a hundred times too thin, which looks entirely plausible and never announces itself. The test has teeth far past its tolerance: ignoring the gradient gives 211 us against 317, a third out. What it deliberately cannot see is the ARRANGEMENT - a drift transit depends only on the integral of n along the path, so any reflection of the profile gives the same answer. That is a property of the physics rather than a weakness to design away, and it is why the unit tests pin the arrangement separately by reversing a ramp and asserting the two differ. The imported field spans the tracked grid exactly, so nothing is extrapolated and no part of the answer is an edge value continued.
